lines: Jamie Alvarez
+1 (555) 010-5820 | jamie.alvarez@example.com | example.com/in/jalvarez
EDUCATION
Riverbend Polytechnic | B.S. in Industrial Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2014 - May 2018
EXPERIENCE
Crestway Foods | Supply Chain Planner | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Jul 2025
- Rebuilt weekly demand planning for 1,400 SKUs across 3 distribution centers with a seasonal forecast model, cutting stockouts from 6.2% to 2.8% while inventory fell by $1.9M.
- Reduced freight costs by 15% by consolidating supplier pickups into regional milk runs.
- Set safety stock for all 1,400 SKUs with the economic order quantity (EOQ) formula, balancing ordering and holding costs.
- Built the weekly supplier scorecard for 40 vendors, which buyers used to renegotiate delivery windows with the five least reliable.
- Led the monthly sales and operations planning meeting, reconciling the sales forecast with plant capacity for the finance and production teams.
- Trained 6 planners on the new forecasting workflow and wrote its exception-handling guide, which the team still uses for promotions.
Lakeview Distribution | Operations Analyst | Metro City, USA | May 2019 - Jan 2021
- Raised forecast accuracy from 70% to 85% by switching the MAPE calculation to cover only SKUs that sold every week.
- Ran a time study of the returns desk; my findings led to a triage station that cut returns processing time from 3 days to 1.
- Writes the dock scheduling rules for 12 carriers, cutting average trailer wait at the dock from 95 to 40 minutes.

- Set up cycle counting for the 2,000 highest-value locations while also covering night-shift supervision, updating the safety training slides, coordinating holiday temp hiring and running the forklift certification schedule, which raised inventory record accuracy from 91% to 98.5%.
PROJECTS
Last-Mile Routing Study | Independent Project | Python | Oct 2024 - Present
- Modeled a regional grocer's 85 daily delivery stops as a vehicle-routing problem, cutting planned route miles 18% against the grocer's current routes.
- Checked the planned routes against 4 weeks of real delivery logs; planned drive times came within 5% of the actual ones.
- Shared the model and a one-page summary with the grocer's dispatch team, who piloted the routes on two trucks for a month.
Regional Food Bank Warehouse | Volunteer Consultant, Team of 4 | Excel | Mar 2022 - Jul 2022
- Analyzed warehouse operations and made recommendations to the food bank's leadership.
- Mapped the donation intake process with the warehouse lead and removed two duplicate data-entry steps, so donations reached the shelves a day sooner.
- Built a seasonal forecast for 1,400 products across three warehouses that more than halved stockouts and cut inventory by nearly $2M.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Python, SAP
Methods: demand forecasting, inventory planning, time studies, vehicle routing

items.says: Check that the profile link works and points to the professional profile you want employers to see.
Move Education below Experience.
items.because: Your recent work is more relevant than a 2018 degree and should be seen first.

items.says: Confirm that the stockout and inventory changes cover the same period and scope as the demand-planning work.
Specify the freight-cost baseline or period and whether the 15% reduction covers all freight or only affected pickups.
items.because: The percentage needs a clear denominator.

items.says: EOQ does not calculate safety stock.
items.because: EOQ determines order quantity, not safety stock.

items.says: Clarify what changed after the five vendors’ delivery windows were renegotiated.
items.because: The bullet stops at use of the scorecard rather than its effect.

items.says: Identify a concrete decision or outcome the sales and operations planning meeting enabled.
items.because: “Led the meeting” alone undersells the work.

items.says: Include evidence of adoption or fewer exceptions if you have it.
Changing which SKUs count does not demonstrate better forecasting.
items.because: Excluding intermittently selling SKUs changes the population being measured rather than showing forecasts improved.

items.says: Clarify whether “3 days to 1” measures elapsed time or hands-on processing time.
Change “Writes” to past tense.
Confirm that the wait-time reduction is attributable to the scheduling rules.
Split or trim the cycle-counting bullet’s unrelated duties.
items.because: They obscure the cycle-counting result and make it unclear which work raised record accuracy.

items.says: Confirm that modeled and current routes used the same stops and constraints.
items.because: Otherwise the 18% savings figure may overstate the opportunity.

items.says: Clarify whether the drive-time check compared the same trips or proposed routes with historical trips.
Add the two-truck pilot’s outcome if you know it.
items.because: Its result is stronger evidence than the fact it happened.

items.says: Remove the analysis-and-recommendations bullet or make it distinct from the next two.
items.because: It is too general to add much on its own.

items.says: Confirm how the one-day improvement was measured.
Confirm whether removing the duplicate steps caused the one-day improvement.
The food-bank forecast result appears to duplicate the Crestway result.
items.because: The product and warehouse counts and the stockout and inventory reductions closely mirror the Crestway bullet.

items.says: Specify your SAP level or relevant applications if that helps match target jobs.
Revisit inventory planning after correcting the EOQ bullet.
Confirm that the project’s “Present” date and the July 2025 role end date are current and accurate.
items.because: The project shows ongoing work after the role ended.
